editorial_note: Canto 11 data remains under full source and translation review. The Sanskrit and English records are draft material tied to the pinned source; phrase coverage and all lexical choices still require chapter-by-chapter verification.
scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for ŚB 11.8.1–11.8.44; the pinned source groups 11.8.20–11.8.21 and 11.8.25–11.8.26.

entries.sanskrit:
अष्टमेऽजगरादिभ्यो नवभ्यः शिक्षितं हरिः ।

अवधूत-गिरा प्राह विवेकायोद्धवं प्रति ॥

प्रारब्ध-कर्म-भोगस्यावश्यं भावित्वात् तद्-अर्थोद्यमैर् नायुर् व्ययो वृथा कर्तव्य इत्य् अजगराच् छिक्षितम् इत्य् आह---सुखम् इत्य्-आदिना । यद् ऐन्द्रियकं सुखं तत् स्वर्गे नरके च भवत्य् एव, यथा दुःखम् । तस्माद् बुद्धस् तन् नेच्छेत ॥१॥
word_for_word: from nine gurus beginning with the python
of the enjoyment of destined karma
because it must come to pass
life should not be wasted uselessly
entries.literal_english: In the eighth chapter Hari speaks through the Avadhūta's words about the nine gurus beginning with the python, for Uddhava's discernment. Since the enjoyment of prārabdha karma must come to pass, one should not waste one's life through efforts made for it. Sensory pleasure exists in heaven and in hell just as pain does; therefore the wise should not desire it.

entries.sanskrit: शरीर-निर्वाह-मात्रं तु यथा-लब्धेन कर्तव्यम् इत्य् आह---ग्रासम् इति । आजगरोऽजगर-वृत्तिः । अक्रिय उदासीनः ॥२॥
word_for_word: only the maintenance of the body
entries.literal_english: Only the maintenance of the body should be undertaken with whatever comes by chance. This is the python's way of life: inactive and indifferent, accepting only a morsel.

entries.sanskrit: यदा नापतति तदा किं कर्तव्यं ? तत्राह---शयीतेति । अनुपक्रमो निरुद्यमः । दिष्ट-भुक् दैवम् एव प्रापकम् इति धैर्यवान् ॥३॥
entries.literal_english: What should be done when food does not arrive? One should lie down, undertaking no effort. The person who eats what destiny provides remains steadfast.

entries.sanskrit: ननु समर्थोऽपि शयीतैव किं ? ॐ इत्य् आह---ओज इति । ओज इन्द्रिय-बलम् । सहो मनो-बलम् । बलं शारीरम् एव । तद् युक्तम् अपि देहम् अकर्मकम् एव बिभ्रच् छयान एव भवेत् । वीत-निद्रः स्वार्थे दत्त-दृष्टिश् च भवेन् न पुनर् ईहेत । इन्द्रियवान् अपीति दर्शनादि-व्यापारम् अपि निवरयति ॥४॥
word_for_word: with attention given to his own aim
entries.literal_english: Even though he is capable, why should he merely lie down? The commentator distinguishes ojas, the power of the senses, saha, the power of the mind, and bala, bodily strength. Even with a sound body he should maintain it while remaining inactive. Free from sleep and keeping his attention on the true aim, he should not strive for acquisition. Even though he has functioning senses, he withdraws their activities such as seeing.

entries.sanskrit: समुद्राच् छिक्षितम् आह---मुनिर् इति । बहिः प्रसन्नश् चासाव् अन्तर् गम्भीरश् च । दुर्विगाह्य एवं-भूत इति परिकलयितुम् अशक्यः, अलक्ष्याभिप्रायत्वात् । दुरत्ययो ऽनतिक्रमणीयः, तेजस्वित्वात् । अनन्त-पारः कालतो देशतश् चापरिच्छेद्यः, स्वरूपाविर्भावात् । अक्षोभ्योऽविकार्यः, रागाद्य्-अभावात् । स्तिमितोदो निश्चलोदकोऽर्णवो यथा तद्वद् एतैर् गुणैर् भवेद् इत्य् अर्थः ॥५॥
word_for_word: without limit in time or space
entries.literal_english: From the ocean the sage learns to be clear outwardly and deep inwardly, difficult to fathom because his intention cannot be discerned, difficult to cross because he is powerful, limitless in time and space because his true nature is manifest, and unperturbed because he lacks passions and other disturbances. He should be like the ocean whose water is still.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, वर्षासु सरिद्भिः समृद्धोऽपि सागरो यथा नोत्सर्पेत, ग्रीष्मे तद्-विहीनोऽपि न शुष्येत । तथा समृद्ध-कामस् तद्-विहीनो वा न हृष्येन् न शोचेद् इत्य् अर्थः । अत्र हेतुः---नारायण-परो न तु विषय-पर इति ॥६॥
entries.literal_english: Although filled by rivers in the rainy season, the ocean does not overflow, and although deprived of them in summer it does not dry up. Likewise, whether rich in desired things or deprived of them, one should neither rejoice nor grieve. The reason is that one is devoted to Nārāyaṇa, not to sense objects.

entries.sanskrit:
रूप-गन्ध-स्पर्श-शब्द-रसैः पञ्चभिर् विषयैर् मोहिताः पतङ्ग-मधुकर-गज-हरिण-मीना हताः, अतस् तेष्व् अनासक्तौ पञ्चैते गुरवः । तद् उक्तम्,
पतङ्ग-मातङ्ग-कुरङ्ग-भृङ्ग-
मीना हताः पञ्चभिर् एव पञ्च ।
एकः प्रमादी स कथं न हन्यते
यः सेवते पञ्चभिर् एव पञ्च ॥ इति ।

तत्र रूप-विलास-मोहितो नश्यतीति पतङ्गाच् छिक्षितम् आह---दृष्ट्वेति । तस्या भावैः प्रलोभितः ॥७॥
entries.literal_english: Moth, bee, elephant, deer, and fish are destroyed after being deluded by the five objects—form, smell, touch, sound, and taste. Therefore these five are gurus in non-attachment. The moth is destroyed by attraction to form and the display of a woman; the commentator cites the fivefold example and says that one who is lured by her features is enticed.

entries.sanskrit: स्त्रियम् उपलक्षणी-कृत्यैतत् प्रपञ्चयति---योषिद् इति ॥८॥
entries.literal_english: Taking a woman as the representative example, he elaborates this teaching about attraction to form and the other sense objects.

entries.sanskrit: मधुकराच् छिक्षितम् आह---स्तोकम् इति । गृहान् गृह-स्थान् अहिंसन्न् अपीडयन् । अयं भावः---यथा मधुकरो विशिश्ट-गन्ध-लोभेनैकस्मिन्न् एव पद्मे वसन्न् अस्त-मय-समये मुकुलिते तस्मिन् बध्यते, एवं मुनिर् अपि गुण-लोभेनैकम् एव गृहम् आश्रितस् तन्-मोहेन बध्यत इति ॥९॥
word_for_word: through greed for a special fragrance
entries.literal_english: From the honeybee he learned to take food little by little without harming households and to practice the honeybee livelihood. Just as a bee, greedy for a particular fragrance, remains in one lotus until it closes at sunset and is trapped, so a sage who becomes greedy for a household's qualities becomes bound by attachment to that home.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, अणुभ्यश् चेति ॥१०॥
entries.literal_english: Moreover, an intelligent person should take the essence from everything—from the smallest and the greatest and from the scriptures—just as the honeybee takes nectar from flowers.

entries.sanskrit: द्वि-विधो मधु-कृत् । मधु कृन्तति पुष्पाद् आच्छिद्य गृह्णातीति मधु-कृद् भ्रमरः । मधु करोत्य् आहारत्वेन स्वरूपेण चेति मधु-मक्षिका च । तत्र प्रथमाच् छिक्षितम् उक्तम्, द्वितीयाच् छिक्षितम् आह---सायम् इदं भोक्ष्यामि, श्व इदं भोक्ष्यामीति भिक्षितम् अन्नादि न सङ्गृह्णीत, किन्तु पाणि-पात्रस् तन्-मात्र-ग्राही । यद् वा, उदरम् एवामत्रं पात्रं यस्य सः । एक-भिक्षायाम् उदर-मात्र-ग्राही भवेत् । सङ्ग्रही तु मक्षिकेव न भवति न जीवतीत्य् अर्थः ॥११॥
word_for_word: the honey-maker is of two kinds
whose belly is the storage vessel
entries.literal_english: The honey-maker is of two kinds: the bee that cuts and gathers honey from flowers, and the honey-making bee. From the latter one learns not to store begged food with the thought, 'I will eat this tonight or tomorrow.' The mendicant should use his hand as a bowl and his belly as the vessel, taking only what fits in one alms-round; he should not become a collector like the bee.

entries.sanskrit: एतद् विवृणोति, पुनः सायन्तनम् इति ॥१२॥
word_for_word: he is destroyed along with it
entries.literal_english: He expands the point: the mendicant should not collect food for the evening or the next day. If he collects like the honeybee, he is destroyed along with that collection.

entries.sanskrit: स्पर्शासक्तिर् नाश-हेतुर् इति गजाच् छिक्षितम् इत्य् आह---पदापीति । पादेनापि दारवीं दारुमयीम् अपि । गजो हि करिणीं प्रदर्श्य निखात-तृण-पिहित-गर्ते निपात्य बध्यते ॥१३॥
word_for_word: causing [the elephant] to fall into a pit
entries.literal_english: Attachment to touch is a cause of destruction, as learned from the elephant. An elephant is trapped even by a wooden female elephant: the hunters display the female, make him fall into a pit covered with grass, and bind him.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, नाधिगच्छेद् इति । नोपगच्छेत् ॥१४॥
entries.literal_english: He adds: one should not approach it.

entries.sanskrit: त्याग-भोग-विहीनो धन-सञ्चयः परगामी भवतीत्य् अत्र मधु-हा गुरुर् इत्य् आह---न देयम् इति । तद् अन्यो बलवान् भुङ्क्ते तद् अप्य् अन्यस् तच् चान्यः । मधु-हा मक्षिकाभिः सञ्चितं मधु यथा भुङ्क्ते तद्वत् । ननु सुगुप्तं धनं कथम् अन्यो ज्ञास्यति हरिष्यति चेति तत्राह---अर्थ-वित् लिङ्गैर् अर्थं तद् उपायं च वेत्तीत्य् अर्थ-वित् । यथा मधु-हा तरु-कोटरादि-गतं मधु वेत्ति हरति च ॥१५॥
word_for_word: one who knows wealth and its signs
honey hidden in a tree hollow
entries.literal_english: The honey-thief teaches that wealth accumulated without renunciation or enjoyment passes to another. Whatever one gathers, another stronger person enjoys, just as the honey-thief consumes honey collected by bees. How can hidden wealth be found and stolen? A knower of wealth knows both the signs of the treasure and the means to obtain it, just as the honey-thief finds and takes honey hidden in a tree hollow.

entries.sanskrit:
स्वोद्यमं विनापि भोगः संभवतीत्य् अत्रापि स एव गुरुर् इत्य् आह---सुदुःखेति। आशासानानाम् इति वक्तव्ये वर्ण-लोप आर्षः ।
यतिश् च ब्रह्मचारी च पक्वान् न स्वामिनाव् उभौ ।
तयोर् अन्नम् अदत्त्वा तु भुक्त्वा चान्द्रायणं चरेत् ॥

इति गृहिणाम् आवश्यकत्वेन दान-विधानात् ॥१६॥
entries.literal_english: The same honey-thief teaches that enjoyment can come even without one's own effort. The source notes that the expression concerning those who hope has an archaic omission, and cites the rule that a householder must give food to a mendicant; if he eats without giving it, he should perform a Cāndrāyaṇa penance.

entries.sanskrit: हरिणाच् छिक्षितम् आह---ग्राम्येति । भगवद्-गीतं तु शृणुयाद् एव । मृगयोर् लुब्धकस्य ॥१७॥
entries.literal_english: From the deer he learned not to listen to worldly songs; one should listen only to the Lord's song. The deer is caught by the hunter through such sound.

entries.sanskrit: हरिण-शब्दाद् एव हरिणी-सुतः ऋष्यशृङ्गोऽपि गुरुर् ज्ञातव्य इत्य् आह---नृत्येति । वश्यो बभूवेति शेषः ॥१८॥
word_for_word: should be understood as a guru
entries.literal_english: From the word 'deer' one should also understand the son of a doe, Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, as a teacher. He became controlled by dancing and the rest; that completion is understood.

entries.sanskrit: रसासक्तिर् नाश-हेतुर् इति मीनाच् छिक्षितम् इत्य् आह---जिह्वयेति । अतिप्रमाथिन्या अतिक्षोभिकया दुर्जयया । ऋच्छति प्राप्नोति । बडिशैर् आमिष-लिप्तैर् लोह-कण्टकैः ॥१९॥
entries.literal_english: Attachment to taste is a cause of destruction, learned from the fish. The tongue is highly agitating and difficult to conquer; the fish meets its death through iron hooks smeared with bait.

entries.sanskrit: दुर्जयत्वम् उपपादयति---इन्द्रियाणीति द्वाभ्याम् । अयं भावः---यद्य् आहारस् त्यज्यते, तर्ह्य् अन्येन्द्रिय-जयः केवलं भवति, रसनेन्द्रियं तु वर्धते । यदि तु भुज्यते, तर्हि पुनश् च रसासक्त्या सर्वेन्द्रिय-क्षोभः स्यात् । अतो रसासक्तिं परित्यज्यौपधवद् भुञ्जीतेति, प्राण-वृत्त्यैव सन्तुष्येद् इत्य् अत्रोक्तम् अपि रसनस्याति-दुर्जयत्व-ज्ञापनायोच्यत इति विशेषः ॥२०-२१॥
word_for_word: he establishes its difficulty to conquer
be satisfied only for the life function
entries.literal_english: He establishes why the tongue is so difficult to conquer. If food is entirely abandoned, the other senses may be conquered but the tongue becomes stronger; if one eats for taste, attachment to taste again agitates every sense. Therefore, abandoning taste-attachment, one should eat only as medicine and be satisfied merely for the maintenance of life.

entries.sanskrit: पिङ्गलाया नैराश्यं शिक्षितम् इति वक्तुं तद्-आख्यानम् आह---पिङ्गलेत्य् आदिना । मे मया शिक्षितम् ॥२२॥
entries.literal_english: To explain that disillusionment with hope was learned from Piṅgalā, he begins her story and says, 'It was learned by me.'

entries.sanskrit: स्वैरिणी काम-चारिणी । सङ्केते रति-स्थाने ॥२३॥
entries.literal_english: A svairiṇī is a woman who moves according to desire; a rendezvous is a place of sexual union.

entries.sanskrit: तान् वित्तवतः सधनान्, अत एव शुल्कदान् मूल्यदान् । कान्तान् सुरतार्हान् ॥२४॥
entries.literal_english: She looked for wealthy men who possessed money and could pay a fee, men who were attractive and suitable for sexual union.

entries.sanskrit: अपिः सम्भावनायाम् । अन्योऽपि माम् उपैष्यत्य् एवं दुराशयेत्य् उत्तरेणान्वयः । द्वार्य् अवलम्बाना पुनः प्रविशती पुनर् निर्गच्छन्ती एवं कुर्वती । निशीथम् अर्घ-रात्रं प्राप ॥२५-२६॥
entries.literal_english: The word 'perhaps' expresses her hope: 'Perhaps another man will approach me.' With this false hope she leaned at the doorway, repeatedly entering and leaving, until midnight—half the night—arrived.

entries.sanskrit: निर्वेदोऽलं-बुद्धिः वित्त-चिन्तैव हेतुर् यस्य सः ॥२७॥
word_for_word: of which she is the one
entries.literal_english: She became disillusioned; her mind reached the conclusion 'enough.' The concern for wealth was the very cause of that disillusionment.

entries.sanskrit: यथा यथावत् । मम मत्तः शृणु । ननु किं निर्विण्णाया गीत-श्रवणेन? तत्राह---हि यस्मात् पुरुषस्याशा-पाशानां निर्वेदोऽसिर् यथा तथा छेत्ता ॥२८॥
entries.literal_english: She says, 'Hear properly from me.' If one asks why a disillusioned woman should sing, the answer is that dispassion is like a sword that cuts the bonds of hope binding a person.

entries.sanskrit: तत्र हेतुः---न हीति । अङ्ग हे राजन् ॥२९॥
entries.literal_english: He gives the reason with 'indeed'; 'O King' is an address to Yadu.

entries.sanskrit: अविजितात्मत्वे हेतुः, याहं बालिशा विवेक-शून्या तस्याः । कुतः ? येन कारणेनासतस् तुच्छान् नरात् कामं कामये ॥३०॥
word_for_word: the reason for lack of self-control
entries.literal_english: The reason for her lack of self-control is that she is foolish and devoid of discernment. She says: for this reason I desire pleasure from a worthless, insignificant man.

entries.sanskrit: बालि-शत्वं प्रपञ्चयति---सन्तम् इति चतुर्भिः । समीपे सन्तम् अन्तर्यामित्वत् । इमम् अपरोक्षम् ईश्वरम् ॥३१॥
word_for_word: because he is the indwelling ruler
entries.literal_english: He elaborates her foolishness in four verses. The Lord is present nearby as the indwelling ruler and is directly perceptible, yet she ignores this Lord.

entries.sanskrit: अतिविगर्ह्या अतिनिन्द्या या वार्ता जीविका, तया । कुतः ? साङ्केत्येन या वृत्तिः, तया । बहुव्रीहिणा स्व-विशेषणं वा । परितापं प्रपञ्चयति--स्त्रैणाद् इति। स्त्री-लम्पटाद् अथ च अर्थ-तृषो लुब्धाद् अत एव अनुशोच्यान् नराद् याहं वित्तं रतिं च इच्छती । मया वृथा आत्मा परितापितः । केन वित्तम् इच्छती ? तेन नरेण क्रीतेन स्वयं विक्रीतेन आत्मना देहेन ॥३२॥
word_for_word: a livelihood through signals and gestures
she desires money and sexual pleasure
with my self sold by myself
entries.literal_english: She has chosen a most censurable livelihood, living by signals and gestures. She desires wealth and sexual pleasure from men who are woman-obsessed, greedy, and pitiable. Thus she has tormented herself uselessly. From whom does she desire wealth? From the very man who buys her, while she herself has sold her own body.

entries.sanskrit: अहो धिङ् मां, याहम् अतिबीभत्सितं भजामीत्य् आह---यद् इति । वंशो नाम स्थूणासु निहितस् तिर्यग् वेणुः । वंश्यास् तस्मिन्न् उभयतो निहिता वेणवः । अस्थिभिर् एव निर्मिता वंशादयो यस्मिंस् तत् । तत्र पृष्ठे दीर्घम् अस्ति यत् स वंशः । पार्श्वास्थीनि वंश्यानि । वंश्यानि स्थूणा हस्त-पादास्थीनि । तथा रोमभिर् नखैश् च पिनद्धं छादितम् । तथापि क्षरन्ति नव-द्वाराणि यस्मिंस् तत् । एवं-भूतागार-रूपं नृ-शरीरम् एतन् मत् मत्तोऽन्या का वा कान्त-बुद्ध्या उपैति सेवते ॥३३॥
entries.literal_english: She laments: 'Shame on me for serving something so repulsive.' The body is compared to a bamboo structure: the spine is the central bamboo, the ribs are the side pieces, it is made of bones, covered with hair and nails, and has nine leaking openings. What woman would approach and serve such a house with the idea that it is a beloved?

entries.sanskrit: सत्-सङ्गतौ सत्याम् अप्य् अहो मम मोह इत्य् आह---विदेहानाम् इति । याहम् असती अच्युताद् अन्यं कामं भोगम् इच्छन्ती, सा ॥३४॥
entries.literal_english: Even though good association was available, she exclaims at her delusion: she, an unchaste woman, desired pleasure from someone other than Acyuta.

entries.sanskrit: एवं निर्विण्णा सती अतः परम् एवं करिष्यामीत्य् आह---सुहृद् इति । अयम् ईश्वरः । आत्मनैव आत्मानम् एव निवेद्य तं विक्रीय विशेषेण क्रीत्वा, अनेनैव सह रमे । रमा लक्ष्मीर् यथा ॥३५॥
entries.literal_english: Having become disillusioned, she says what she will do next: this Lord is the true friend. By offering herself to the Self alone, selling herself to Him and especially purchasing Him, she will delight with Him, as Lakṣmī delights with the Lord.

entries.sanskrit: अन्यस्यासेव्यत्वं दर्शयति---कियद् इति । आद्यन्तवन्तो ये कामा विषयाः काम-दा नरा वा देवा वा काल-कलिता भार्यायाः कियत् प्रियं कृतवन्तः ? न किञ्चित् । अतो नेहामुत्र च तद्-व्यतिरिक्तः कोऽपि सेव्योऽस्तीत्य् अर्थः ॥३६॥
entries.literal_english: He shows why no other person is worthy of service. Sense objects and the men or gods who grant them have beginnings and ends and are conquered by time. What real benefit have they given the wife? Nothing. Therefore no one other than the Lord is worthy of service either here or hereafter.

entries.sanskrit: एवं निश्चित्य स्व-भाग्यम् अभिनन्दति---नूनम् इति । दुष्टा आशा यस्यास् तस्या मे॥३७॥
entries.literal_english: Having decided this, she congratulates herself on her fortune: surely the corrupt hope that belonged to me has now been destroyed.

entries.sanskrit: ननु धनाप्राप्त्या क्लिष्टासि, कथं विष्णुः प्रीतः ? तत्राह---मैवम् इति । मन्द-भाग्य चेद् अहं स्यां तर्ह्य् एव निर्वेद-हेतवः क्लेशा न स्युर् इत्य् अर्थः । येन निर्वेदेन अनुबन्धं गृहादिकं निर्हृत्य परित्यज्य ॥३८॥
entries.literal_english: An objection is raised: 'You are distressed because wealth was not obtained; how then has Viṣṇu shown favor?' She answers: 'Do not think so. If I were unfortunate, these sufferings that produce dispassion would not have arisen. Through this dispassion I have removed and abandoned attachment to the house and the rest.'

entries.sanskrit: अतस् तेन श्री-विष्णुनोपकृतं कृतम् उपकारं निर्वेद-लक्षणम् । ग्राम्येषु नरेषु विषयेषु वा सङ्गताः ॥३९॥
entries.literal_english: Thus Śrī Viṣṇu has done her a favor: He has given her dispassion. She had been attached to worldly men and to sense objects.

entries.sanskrit: कथं व्रजसि तद् आह---सन्तुष्टेति ॥४०॥
entries.literal_english: How will you proceed? He answers with the teaching that, having become satisfied, she will no longer return to that life.

entries.sanskrit: ननु ब्रह्मादीन् हित्वा अमुनैवेति कोऽयं नियमस् तत्राह---संसारेति । मुषितेक्षणम् अपहृत-विवेकम् ॥४१॥
word_for_word: having left Brahmā and the others
one whose vision has been stolen
whose discernment has been taken away
entries.literal_english: Why should she leave Brahmā and the others and choose this Lord alone? The answer is that saṃsāra steals the vision and removes discernment; therefore the individual should seek the Lord rather than another limited object.

entries.sanskrit: तर्हि किम् आत्म-त्राणोपाधिना तं भजिष्यसि, न, तत्र सर्वतो निर्विद्य भगवद्-भजने प्रवृत्तस्यात्मन एव समर्थत्वाद् इत्य् आह---आत्मैवेति । यदा एवं जगत् पश्येत् ततश् चाप्रमतः सन्निखिलाद् इहामुत्र च भोगान् निर्विद्येत तदा ह्य् आत्मनैवात्मनो गोप्तेत्य् अन्वयः । अतः केवलं प्रेम्णैव भजामीति भावः ॥४२॥
word_for_word: with a separate means of self-protection
of one engaged in worship of Bhagavān
by the Self alone, of oneself
entries.literal_english: Should she worship Him with a separate device for protecting herself? No. For one who has become dispassionate toward everything and has entered Bhagavān's worship, the Self alone is capable of protecting the self. When one sees the world in this way and becomes vigilant, one becomes dispassionate toward all enjoyments here and hereafter; therefore she says, 'I will worship Him through love alone.'

entries.sanskrit: कान्तस्य तर्षोऽभिलाषस् ततो जातम् ।
entries.literal_english: The longing and desire for the beloved arose from that [newly awakened devotion].

entries.sanskrit: फलितम् आह---आशा हीति ।
entries.literal_english: He states the result: hope is the cause of suffering, while freedom from such worldly hope is happiness.
